chapter.title: Step 1: Check Market Regime
chapter.subtitle: 30 seconds to know what kind of market you're in

slides.title: VIX-Based Regime Detection (Google It)
rows: Oversold bounces in quality names only

steps.title: Google 'VIX index'
steps.description: The current VIX value appears instantly. Note: below 18 = green light, above 28 = red alert.

steps.title: Check S&P 500 trend
steps.description: Is SPY above or below its 50-day moving average? Above = bullish, below = bearish.

steps.title: Note the regime
steps.description: Write it at the top of today's screening notes. This determines WHICH Finviz preset you run.

slides.title: Why Regime Matters for Your Screens
slides.text: In Risk-On, you run the Momentum and Breakout screeners. In Risk-Off, you ONLY run the Oversold Bounce screener targeting defensive sectors. In Neutral, you run all three. Skipping this step is the number one reason DIY screeners fail — they run momentum screens in a crash and get destroyed.

chapter.title: Strategy 1: Oversold Bounce
chapter.subtitle: Finding beaten-down stocks ready to snap back

slides.title: The Oversold Bounce Logic
slides.text: When a quality stock gets hammered and its RSI drops below 35, it's statistically likely to bounce. We filter for stocks with high volume on the drop — that means institutions are stepping in. Add a market cap floor to avoid penny stocks, and you have a reliable mean-reversion setup.

steps.title: Go to finviz.com/screener.ashx
steps.description: Click the 'Technical' tab at the top of the screener.

steps.title: RSI (14) → Oversold (below 30)
steps.description: Or select 'Under 40' for more results. This is your core oversold filter.

steps.title: Relative Volume → Over 1.5
steps.description: This ensures volume is at least 50% above normal — institutions are trading.

steps.title: Market Cap → Mid ($2B to $10B) or Large (over $10B)
steps.description: Avoid micro-caps. Quality names only for oversold bounces.

steps.title: Average Volume → Over 500K
steps.description: Ensures liquidity. You need to be able to exit easily.

steps.title: Click 'Charts' view
steps.description: Scan the charts visually. Look for a clear drop followed by a volume spike — that's your signal.

slides.title: Finviz Filter Summary: Oversold Bounce
rows: Stock is beaten down, bounce likely
Enough liquidity to enter and exit

slides.title: Pro Tip: Save Your Finviz Presets
slides.text: Finviz saves your filter URL in the browser address bar. Bookmark each strategy as a separate bookmark. Tomorrow, just click the bookmark and the exact same filters load instantly. Label them: 'MW Oversold', 'MW Momentum', 'MW Breakout'. Three clicks, three screens, done in 5 minutes.

slides.question: You run the Oversold Bounce screener and find a stock with RSI 25, relative volume 3.2, but market cap is $180M. Should you trade it?
choices: Yes — the RSI and volume are perfect
No — market cap too small, high manipulation risk
Yes — small caps have bigger bounces
Maybe — check the news first
slides.explanation: A $180M market cap stock is a micro-cap. These are easily manipulated, have poor liquidity, and are often targets of pump-and-dump schemes. Stick to the $2B+ market cap filter. Quality over excitement.

chapter.title: Strategy 2: Momentum Expansion
chapter.subtitle: Riding stocks that are already moving up — with volume proof

slides.title: The Momentum Logic
slides.text: Momentum trading means buying strength. A stock trading above its 20-day moving average with double its normal volume is telling you: big money is coming in. The RSI between 50 and 75 confirms the move has room to run — it's not yet overbought. This is the bread-and-butter strategy in Risk-On markets.

steps.title: 20-Day SMA → Price above SMA20
steps.description: In Finviz Technical tab: '20-Day Simple Moving Average' → 'Price above SMA20'. Confirms uptrend.

steps.title: Relative Volume → Over 2
steps.description: Volume at least double normal. This is the 'expansion' — money is flooding in.

steps.title: RSI (14) → 50 to 70 or Not Overbought
steps.description: Sweet spot: strong enough to confirm momentum, not so high it's about to reverse.

steps.title: Market Cap → Mid or Large
steps.description: Same liquidity filter as before. No micro-caps.

steps.title: Change → Up
steps.description: In the Descriptive tab, set 'Change' to 'Up' to see only stocks green today.

steps.title: Sort by 'Relative Volume' descending
steps.description: The highest volume surge stocks appear first — those have the strongest momentum signal.

slides.title: Finviz Filter Summary: Momentum
rows: Can enter and exit without slippage

slides.title: When NOT to Run Momentum Screens
slides.text: If the VIX is above 28 and the S and P 500 is below its 50-day moving average, do NOT run this screener. Momentum strategies in Risk-Off markets produce false signals constantly. Everything looks like a bounce until it drops another 5%. Save this strategy for green regimes only.

chapter.title: Strategy 3: Breakout Squeeze
chapter.subtitle: Catching stocks exploding through resistance with expanding volatility

slides.title: The Breakout Logic
slides.text: A breakout happens when a stock that's been consolidating near resistance finally pushes through with conviction. The key confirmation is expanding volatility — measured by ATR — combined with the price clearing the 50-day moving average. In Finviz terms: new highs on high volume above a key moving average.

steps.title: 50-Day SMA → Price above SMA50
steps.description: Confirms the stock is in a medium-term uptrend. Not just a dead-cat bounce.

steps.title: New High/Low → New High
steps.description: In the Technical tab, select 'New High'. The stock is breaking out right now.

steps.title: Relative Volume → Over 1.5
steps.description: Breakout on low volume is a fake-out. High volume confirms institutional participation.

steps.title: Volatility → Week: Over 3%
steps.description: In Technical tab, set weekly volatility above 3%. This is the 'squeeze' — volatility expanding.

steps.title: Market Cap → Small ($300M-$2B) or Mid/Large
steps.description: Breakouts work across all cap sizes. Small caps have bigger moves but more risk.

steps.title: Review charts manually
steps.description: Look for a clear consolidation pattern (flag, triangle, range) that just broke. That's your entry.

slides.title: Finviz Filter Summary: Breakout
rows: Volume confirms the breakout is real

slides.title: Bonus: Finviz 'TA' Column Trick
slides.text: In the screener results, click 'TA' view (Technical Analysis). Finviz shows you the chart with all indicators overlaid — SMA lines, volume bars, RSI. You can visually confirm the breakout pattern in 3 seconds without opening another tool. If the chart looks messy or the breakout is weak, skip it. Clean charts, clean trades.

slides.question: A stock is at a new 52-week high with relative volume of 0.6 (BELOW average). Is this a valid breakout?
choices: Yes — new highs are always bullish
No — low volume breakouts are unreliable and often reverse
Yes — volume doesn't matter for breakouts
Maybe — wait for volume to pick up tomorrow
slides.explanation: A breakout on low volume is one of the most common false signals in trading. Without institutional participation (volume surge), the breakout lacks conviction and frequently reverses within days. Always require relative volume above 1.5 for breakout trades.

chapter.title: Scoring & Selection
chapter.subtitle: How to pick the Top 5 from your screener results — manually

slides.title: Simplified 3-Factor Scoring
slides.text: Our automated scanner uses 4 factors. For your manual version, we simplify to 3 factors you can evaluate in 60 seconds per stock. Technical setup quality, volume confirmation, and chart clarity. Each factor is scored 1 to 3. Total score: 3 to 9. Only trade setups scoring 7 or above.

slides.title: DIY Scoring Sheet (3 Factors × 1-3 Points)
rows: RSI borderline, price barely above MA
RSI clear signal, price above 1 MA
RSI perfect zone, above both SMA20+50

steps.title: Run all 3 screeners
steps.description: Open your 3 bookmarked Finviz URLs. Takes 30 seconds.

steps.title: Collect candidates
steps.description: Note every stock that appears. Typically 10-30 results across all 3 screens.

steps.title: Quick chart check
steps.description: Open the Finviz chart for each. Spend 15 seconds per chart. Eliminate ugly charts immediately.

steps.title: Score the survivors
steps.description: Apply the 3-factor scoring to remaining candidates. Takes 1 minute per stock.

steps.title: Pick Top 5
steps.description: Sort by total score. Take the top 5 that score 7 or above. These are your signals for tomorrow.

slides.title: The Dilution Check (30 Seconds, Non-Negotiable)
slides.text: For EVERY stock in your Top 5, do a quick dilution check. Google the ticker plus 'dilution' or 'offering'. If you see any mention of ATM offering, warrants, shelf registration, or a recent S-3 filing in the last 90 days — REMOVE IT from your list immediately. This 30-second check saved us from the INDO disaster where a perfect technical setup got crushed by a surprise dilution.

slides.title: How to Set Entry, Stop, and Targets

levels.label: Entry
levels.value: Previous day's close or limit within 1%

levels.label: Stop Loss
levels.value: Below the nearest support or −6 to 8%

levels.label: Timeout
levels.value: Close after 5 trading days if no exit hit

slides.question: Your screener returns 20 results. After chart review and scoring, 3 stocks score 8/9 and 7 stocks score 5-6/9. How many do you trade?
choices: All 10 — diversification is key
Only the 3 scoring 8 or above — quality over quantity
The top 7 — anything above 5 is tradeable
None — wait for a day with more 9/9 scores
slides.explanation: Only trade setups scoring 7 or above. The 3 stocks scoring 8/9 are your A-grade picks. The 5-6 scores lack sufficient confluence and have a much lower success rate. Patience and selectivity are your edge.

slides.title: Position Sizing: The Simple Rule
slides.text: Decide how many slots you want. We recommend 4 for most people. Divide your trading capital by 4. That's your position size. If you have ten thousand dollars, each trade gets twenty-five hundred. When a position closes, the cash returns to the pool. When you open a new position, use the same fixed amount. Don't increase size after a win. Don't decrease after a loss. Consistency is the entire game.

TP1 alert fires → Sell 50%, move stop to breakeven
TP2 alert fires → Sell remaining 50%

Down 3% but stop not hit → Trust your stop level
News is scary but stock is fine → Ignore the noise
A friend says 'sell' → Follow your system, not opinions

slides.title: When Do Your Results Match Ours?
slides.text: After about 10 trading days of following this system consistently, your results will start to resemble the Market Watch scanner's performance. Why? Because you're using the same core logic: regime-aware screening, volume-confirmed entries, mechanical exits, and fixed position sizing. The automated version is faster and covers more tickers, but the edge comes from the PROCESS, not the technology.

Bookmark 3 Finviz screener presets (Oversold, Momentum, Breakout)
Run regime-appropriate screens each evening (5 minutes)
Score results with 3-factor system, pick Top 5 scoring 7+
Quick dilution check: Google 'TICKER dilution' for each pick
Log everything in Google Sheets (date, entry, stop, TP1, TP2, timeout)
Set Yahoo/Webull alerts for stop loss and TP1 on every position
Position size = total capital ÷ 4 slots, fixed amount each trade
At TP1: sell 50%, trail stop to breakeven
At timeout (day 5): close regardless of P&L
Review your spreadsheet weekly — calculate win rate and profit factor
Never cherry-pick, never skip stops, follow the system

slides.title: The Secret? It's Not the Tool. It's the Process.
slides.text: Professional traders don't win because they have better software. They win because they have a PROCESS they follow every single day without exception. You now have that process. Three screeners, a scoring sheet, a spreadsheet tracker, and ironclad exit rules. Fifteen minutes a day, zero cost, same edge. The rest is discipline. Go build your system.

slides.question: What is the single biggest advantage of building your own DIY scanner vs using a paid signal service?
choices: It's cheaper
You understand WHY every trade is taken, building real trading skill
You get more signals
The signals are better quality
slides.explanation: The biggest advantage isn't the cost savings — it's the education. When you build and run the screens yourself, you understand the logic behind every trade. If a trade fails, you know why. If the market changes, you can adapt. A paid signal service keeps you dependent. Your DIY system makes you independent. That's the real edge.
